questions.stem: A company manufactures aluminium cans. They want to reduce their carbon footprint. Which action would have the greatest impact?

options.text: Painting the factory a lighter colour
Using recycled aluminium instead of extracting new aluminium from ore, as recycling uses about 5% of the energy
Changing the shape of the cans
Moving the factory to a different country

questions.explanation: Extracting aluminium from its ore (bauxite) by electrolysis is extremely energy-intensive. Recycling aluminium uses only about 5% of the energy, dramatically reducing CO₂ emissions from electricity generation. This is one of the most effective ways to reduce a carbon footprint in manufacturing — the energy savings are enormous because you skip the electrolysis step.

questions.stem: A family is comparing two options to reduce their household carbon footprint: switching from a petrol car to an electric car, or installing solar panels. Which consideration is most important for the electric car option?

options.text: Electric cars have no carbon footprint at all
The carbon footprint reduction depends on how the electricity used to charge the car is generated
Electric cars produce more CO₂ than petrol cars
The colour of the car affects its carbon footprint

questions.explanation: An electric car charged using electricity from coal-fired power stations may have a similar carbon footprint to a petrol car. However, if the electricity comes from renewable sources (wind, solar, nuclear), the carbon footprint is much lower. The overall benefit depends on the energy mix of the electricity grid. Manufacturing the battery also has a carbon cost that must be considered.

questions.stem: A carbon footprint includes both direct and indirect emissions. For a loaf of bread, which would count as an indirect emission?

options.text: CO₂ from baking the bread in the oven
CO₂ from transporting the bread to the shop
CO₂ from manufacturing the fertiliser used to grow the wheat
All of the above contribute to the carbon footprint

questions.explanation: A carbon footprint includes all greenhouse gas emissions across a product's entire life cycle: growing raw materials (including fertiliser production), manufacturing, packaging, transportation, use, and disposal. This 'cradle to grave' approach means even seemingly small items like bread have a significant total carbon footprint when all stages are considered.

questions.stem: Carbon offsetting involves compensating for CO₂ emissions by funding projects that reduce CO₂ elsewhere. An airline offers passengers the option to 'offset' their flight emissions by planting trees. Why might scientists be cautious about this approach?

options.text: Trees do not absorb carbon dioxide
Trees take decades to absorb the CO₂ that was released instantly by the flight, and may be cut down or burned before fully offsetting the emissions
Carbon offsetting always works perfectly
Airlines do not produce significant CO₂ emissions

questions.explanation: The CO₂ from a flight is released immediately into the atmosphere, but a tree takes 20-50 years to absorb an equivalent amount. During that time, the CO₂ is contributing to warming. Trees may also be felled, burned in wildfires, or die from disease before fully offsetting the carbon. Reducing emissions is more effective than offsetting them after the fact.

questions.stem: Two countries produce the same total CO₂ emissions, but Country A has a population of 10 million while Country B has a population of 100 million. Which measurement would better reflect the impact per citizen?

options.text: Total national emissions — both countries are equally responsible
Emissions per capita (per person) — Country A has 10 times the emissions per person
Emissions per square kilometre of land
Emissions per GDP

questions.explanation: Emissions per capita (per person) is a fairer comparison of individual impact. Country A's citizens each produce 10 times as much CO₂ as Country B's citizens on average. While total national emissions matter for global targets, per capita figures better reflect lifestyle choices and help identify where individual reductions could be most effective.
